quirks: Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld from 1677 to 1884. All Meland church records (baptisms, marriages, burials) for 1770-1820 are recorded in the Hamre kirkebøker, not in a separate Meland register. Search Hamre prestegjeld books (FamilySearch Catalog 47267) — there is no independent Meland clerical series until the Alversund prestegjeld was formed in 1885.

Meland marriages are expected to appear in the Meland annex section within the Hamre kirkebøk. The 1750-1857 volume organizes entries by parish. The marriage should be under the Meland entries, not the main Hamre parish section.

The national FamilySearch 'Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926' index (collection 1468080) is explicitly a legacy partial index — not complete for any place or period, and farm names (gårdnames) were not indexed. A negative result does not mean the marriage is absent; always verify in the original Hamre kirkebøk images.

Start with the compiled name extracts before browsing the original: FamilySearch Catalog no. 261335 (Register over døpte, gifte og begravede, utdrag av Hamre kirkebok nr. 1 & 3; Hamre kirkebok nr. 2, compiled by Haarstad and Luker) is a hand-compiled name register and the fastest first-pass search tool for 1677-1826.

Norwegian patronymic naming was universal in this period. 'Monsen' = son of Mons; 'Halsteinsdatter' = daughter of Halstein. Surnames changed every generation. Women did not take their husband's patronymic at marriage in this era — Unna would continue to appear in records as 'Halsteinsdatter' after marriage.
Farm names (e.g., Hestdal) are addresses/residences, not hereditary surnames. They should not be searched as part of a surname field. A person who moved farms changed their 'farm name' identifier.

Couples were usually married in the bride's home parish. Since Unna Halsteinsdatter was from Hestdal, Meland, the marriage entry should appear in the Meland section of the Hamre register, not the main Hamre section.

Civil registration in Norway did not begin until 1876 (national level) and 1915 (community Folkeregistre). For 1770-1820 there are no civil vital records — the Lutheran parish register is the only vital record source.

The 1801 census (FamilySearch collection 3733603; also at Digitalarkivet) is the only full-household nominative census within or immediately bracketing the 1770-1820 window. Earlier counts (1664-1666, 1701) list males only. The 1801 census will show the family's composition and ages, bracketing the likely marriage date.

Some Meland farms (including possibly Hestdal) belonged to the Lysekloster Estate; if probate for a Meland family is not found in the Nordhordaland sorenskriveri records, also check Hardanger og Voss sorenskriveri where Lysekloster probates were kept.

Pre-1814 kirkebøk entries are in Danish-influenced Norwegian written in Gothic (Kurrent-influenced) script. Key marriage vocabulary: viede/vigde/copulerede (married), trolovelse (betrothal/engagement), lysning (banns), ungkarl (bachelor), pige (maiden), enke/enkemand (widow/widower).

The Digitalarkivet browse interface (https://media.digitalarkivet.no/kb/browse) provides browse-only access to the 1750-1857 Hamre volume — no online name index. Images must be paged through manually by the researcher.

The three-volume bygdebøk 'Mellom bakkar og berg: gard og ætt i Meland' (Kleiveland & Homlong) covers all 50 Meland farms including Hestdal (farm no. 30) with genealogical reconstructions from the 1500s to 2004. It is the most comprehensive secondary source and should be consulted in parallel with original records.

Elna Fløisand Luker's 'Melands slekter' (FamilySearch Library 948.32/M1 D2) is a compiled genealogy drawing on the Hamre church books, Nordhordaland probate protocols, and mortgage registers — a critical secondary finding aid for Meland families.

# Locality Guide: Hamre Prestegjeld (Meland / Hamre Parishes), Søndre Bergenhus, Norway (1770–1820)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Ecclesiastical unit:** Hamre prestegjeld (clerical district), Diocese of Bjørgvin (continuous from 1538). Meland was an annex parish within Hamre prestegjeld from 1677 through 1884.
- **Civil administrative unit during 1770–1820:** Søndre Bergenhus amt (Bergenhus amt until 1763; Hordaland fylke only from 1919). Sorenskriveri: Nordhordland. Fogderi: Nordhordland.
- **Location:** Hamre church on Osterøy island; Meland parish on Holsnøy island; both northeast/northwest of Bergen.
- **Population:** Hordaland province ~78,600–78,900 in 1801 (Populstat). No parish-level figure available from tools.
- **Economy:** Subsistence farming, coastal fishing, coastal trade.
- **Religion:** Exclusively Lutheran state church.

## Boundary changes

- **Before 1885:** Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld. All church records for Meland from 1677 to 1884 are in the Hamre kirkebøker.
- **1885:** Alversund and Meland separated from Hamre prestegjeld into the new Alversund prestegjeld.
- **1749:** Hosanger, Mo, and Seim separated from Hamre — does not affect Meland research.
- **Civil:** Meland's tinglag was Alversund (distinct from Hamre tinglag), relevant for land/mortgage searches.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **No civil registration existed in 1770–1820.** Civil registration began nationally in 1876; community Folkeregistre began in 1915.
- The Lutheran parish register (kirkebøk) is the only vital record source for this period.

### Church records (kirkebøker) — PRIMARY SOURCE

**Key volumes for 1770–1820:**
- Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Meland Parish Church Records 1750–1857 at Digitalarkivet (browse-only images)
- Kirkebøker, 1677–1928 — Hamre prestegjeld, FamilySearch Catalog no. 47267 (images)
- Extract of christenings and marriages 1677–1826 — Hamre, FamilySearch Catalog no. 209228
- Register over døpte, gifte og begravede (compiled index by Haarstad/Luker), FamilySearch Catalog no. 261335 — USE THIS FIRST
- Hamre döde 1762–1826 (Luker), FamilySearch Catalog no. 769257

**Indexed national collections:**
- Norway, Marriages, 1660–1926 (FamilySearch ID 1468080) — partial legacy index only; verify in originals
- Norway, Baptisms, 1634–1927 (ID 1467014) — index only
- Norway, Burials, 1666–1927 (ID 1468081) — index only
- Norway, Church Books, 1797–1958 (ID 4237104) — indexed + images (covers from 1797)

**Digitization level:** Digitalarkivet images = browse-only. FamilySearch Catalog films = images (login/FHC). Compiled extracts (261335) = most practical indexed finding aid for 1770–1820.

**Language:** Danish/Norwegian; Gothic script. Records are not in English.

**What a marriage entry contains (pre-1814):** names, marriage date, ages, residences (farm names), status (bachelor/maiden/widower/widow), occupations, two bondsmen names, three banns dates, sometimes engagement date.

### Census records
- **1801 census** — only full-household nominative census in target window. FamilySearch collection 3733603 (indexed + images); Digitalarkivet; covers Meland.
- Manntall i Meland sogn (Hamre prestegjeld), FamilySearch Catalog 277046, covers 1645, 1666, 1701, 1801, 1865, 1900.
- No census 1770–1800; 1664–1666 and 1701 counts list males only.

### Probate records
- Skifteprotokoller 1702–1910, Nordhordaland sorenskriveri, FamilySearch Catalog 438738
- Skifteprotokoller 1773–1810, Nordhordland Prosti (clerical probate), FamilySearch Catalog 438920
- Probate Index Cards 1640–1903, FamilySearch collection 1661306 (name-indexed)
- Note: some Meland farms under Lysekloster Estate — if not found in Nordhordaland, check Hardanger og Voss sorenskriveri

### Land records
- Pantebøker 1741–1893, Nordhordaland, FamilySearch Catalog 494924 (browse-only images)
- Meland's tinglag: Alversund (search separately from Hamre tinglag)

### Court records
- Tingbøker 1642–1701, Nordhordaland sorenskriveri, FamilySearch Catalog (film 505971) — predates target window
- Post-1701 court minutes: Digitalarkivet, Nordhordaland sorenskriveri

### Compiled genealogies and farm books
- 'Mellom bakkar og berg: gard og ætt i Meland' (Kleiveland & Homlong) — covers all 50 Meland farms including Hestdal (farm no. 30), 1500s to 2004. FamilySearch Library 948.32/M1 D2
- Luker, Elna Fløisand: 'Melands slekter' — families from Hamre church books, probate, and mortgage records. FamilySearch Library 948.32/M1 D2
- Alenfit skibreide (downloadable PDF) — farm owners in Alversund, Sæbø, Lygra, Seim, Hamre parishes to 1814

### Military records
- Norwegian military records for Nordhordland 1770–1820 not cataloged in FamilySearch tool results; consult Arkivverket (https://www.arkivverket.no) for legd/infantry muster rolls.

### Tax records
- Norway Accounting and Tax Records at Digitalarkivet (https://www.digitalarkivet.no/content/85/regnskap-og-skatt); browse-only images
- Extra Tax (Ekstraskatt) 1762–1772 falls just before the window

### Cemetery records
- Burial register is part of the kirkebøk ('Begravede' or 'Døde' section)
- BillionGraves and FindAGrave have limited coverage for early rural Hordaland

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Digitalarkivet (National Archives) | Hamre kirkebøker 1750–1857 (browse-only); 1801 census; probate/land/court records | Free — https://digitalarkivet.no |
| FamilySearch | Catalog nos. 47267, 209228, 261335, 769257; collections 1468080, 1467014, 1468081, 3733603, 4237104 | Free |
| Ancestry | Norway Marriages, Births/Christenings, 1801 Census | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Norway Marriages, Baptisms, 1801 Census | Subscription |
| RHD (Norwegian Historical Data Centre) | Parish record search; census search | Free — https://rhd.uit.no |

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Statsarkivet i Bergen (Bergen Regional State Archive) | Original Hamre kirkebøker; Nordhordaland records | In-person; some digitized |
| National Archives of Norway (Arkivverket) | Military, tax, probate, court records | In-person / https://www.arkivverket.no |
| FamilySearch Family History Library | Microfilm of catalog nos. 47267, 261335, etc. | Via local FamilySearch Centers |

## Records NOT online (as name-searchable indexes)
- Hamre kirkebøk 1750–1857 Meland section: browse-only images at Digitalarkivet, no name index
- Tax and accounting records for Nordhordland 1770–1820: images at Digitalarkivet, not name-indexed
- Military muster rolls for Nordhordland: not available in tool results; physical/Arkivverket search required
- Court minute books (tingbøker) post-1701: images at FamilySearch Catalog and Digitalarkivet, not name-indexed

## Known record losses
No known record losses documented in FamilySearch Wiki tool results for Hamre or Meland parishes. The continuous kirkebøk series from 1677 appears intact.

## Research tips
1. Search Hamre prestegjeld books — Meland had no independent register before 1885.
2. Use compiled extracts (FamilySearch Catalog 261335) first — fastest path to a named entry in 1770–1820.
3. The national Marriages index (1468080) is a partial legacy index; always verify in originals.
4. Patronymics were universal: 'Monsen' = son of Mons; 'Halsteinsdatter' = daughter of Halstein. Women retained birth patronymics after marriage.
5. Farm names are addresses, not hereditary surnames — do not search them as surnames.
6. Marriage should appear in the Meland annex section of the Hamre book (bride's home parish).
7. Pre-1814 entries vary in detail by pastor; the printed-form standard came only in 1814.
8. Unna (b. 1745) may have been previously married — the entry would note her as enke (widow).
9. Cross-check the 1801 census: children's ages will bracket the likely marriage year.
10. Use the Meland bygdebøker ('Mellom bakkar og berg') — Hestdal is farm no. 30, covered in detail.
11. If probate search needed: check Nordhordaland sorenskriveri (catalog 438738) and clerical probate (438920); if Meland farm was under Lysekloster Estate, also check Hardanger og Voss sorenskriveri.
12. Records are in Danish/Norwegian Gothic script. Key terms: viede/vigde (married), trolovelse (betrothal), lysning (banns), ungkarl (bachelor), pige (maiden), enke/enkemand (widow/widower).

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter

**Research Question:** When and where did Anders Monsen (born 7 April 1759, Meland/Hamre area, Hordaland, Norway) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born 27 May 1745, Hestdal, Meland, Hordaland, Norway), and what does the marriage record show?

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter were married on **25 June 1786** at **Hamre, Hordaland, Norway**. This finding rests on a derivative marriage index entry corroborated by geographic evidence from the 1801 census. The original Hamre kirchenbuch entry has not yet been read; the 'what does the record show' component of the question is partially answered.

---

### Sources and Evidence

**Primary evidence: Marriage index entry (src_001)**

The FamilySearch database "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" (collection 1468080), a derivative partial index compiled from original Lutheran parish registers, contains an entry for the marriage of Anders Monsen and "Urna Halsteinsdr" on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway.^1 This collection is explicitly described by FamilySearch as a legacy partial index — not complete for any place or period — and does not transcribe the full content of the original entry (banns dates, bondsmen, bride's marital status, farm names). The indexed entry is therefore a **derivative source** carrying **primary information** about the marriage event, because the underlying data was recorded by the officiating Lutheran pastor at the time of the ceremony, a contemporaneous witness.

^1 "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2 : accessed 12 October 2026), entry for Anders Monsen and Urna Halsteinsdr, 25 June 1786; citing Hamre kirkebøk 1750-1857, Meland annex section, Digitalarkivet.

**Bride's name — transcription artifact, not error**

The indexed bride name "Urna Halsteinsdr" differs from the tree name "Unna Halsteinsdatter" in two ways that are both documented systematic transcription patterns for this collection. First, the medial consonant: Gothic (Kurrent-influenced) script forms for 'n' can be misread as 'r' by indexers unfamiliar with the letterform, producing "Urna" from "Unna." Second, the suffix: the patronymic ending "-datter" was abbreviated to "-dr" in the index. These are known collection-level artifacts. The structured value in assertion a_003 correctly recovers the intended name as Unna Halsteinsdatter. The underlying identity of the bride is not in doubt; the original Hamre kirkebøk should be consulted to confirm the correct spelling as written.

**Corroborating geographic evidence: 1801 census (src_002)**

The 1801 Norwegian census (FamilySearch, "Norges folketelling, 1801", collection 3733603) contains a household headed by Nils Andersen in Hamre prestegjeld, Hordaland, in which an Anders Monsen with birth year 1758 appears as a member.^2 The 1-year birth-year discrepancy (1758 in the census vs. established birth year of 7 April 1759) is well within the normal range of age rounding in 18th-century Norwegian census enumeration. The same-person score of 0.793 reflects strong corroboration of the core identifiers — name, sex, and place. This record establishes that an Anders Monsen was resident in Hamre prestegjeld in 1801, the same parish where the 1786 marriage occurred, which is geographically consistent with the marriage record.

^2 "Norges folketelling, 1801," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:8YMV-R76Z : accessed 12 October 2026), entry for Anders Monsen in household of Nils Andersen, Hamre prestegjeld, Hordaland, Norway.

The 1801 census does not independently attest the 1786 marriage event (date, place, or parties). It corroborates only that an Anders Monsen was residing in the correct parish fifteen years after the marriage. The household's wife position is occupied by Borni Nilsdatter (b. ~1744), not Unna Halsteinsdatter, which raises a secondary research question about Unna's fate between 1786 and 1801 — she may have died and Anders may have remarried, or this may be a different Anders Monsen entirely. This question lies outside the scope of q_001's core marriage facts and is documented in assertions a_020, a_022, and a_024 without constituting a registered conflict on the 1786 marriage date, place, or parties.

---

### Identity Correlation

The groom in the marriage index entry (a_001) is identified as Anders Monsen by exact name match, correct Hordaland region, and age-appropriate date (approximately 27 at marriage, consistent with birth in 1759). Person-evidence pe_001 and pe_005 link the groom's name and marriage assertions to tree person LKFW-9XH at confident level.

The bride in the marriage index entry (a_003) is identified as Unna Halsteinsdatter — once the transcription artifact is corrected — by exact name match (given name Unna, patronymic Halsteinsdatter), correct Hordaland region, and spousal pairing with the identified groom. Person-evidence pe_003 and pe_007 link the bride's name and marriage assertions to tree person KZHH-VTX at confident level, with a same-person score of 0.904.

---

### What the Record Shows

The derivative index entry (src_001) records:
- **Groom:** Anders Monsen
- **Bride:** Urna Halsteinsdr (= Unna Halsteinsdatter; transcription artifact documented above)
- **Marriage date:** 25 June 1786
- **Marriage place:** Hamre, Hordaland, Norway (Meland annex section of the Hamre kirkebøk, consistent with the bride's Hestdal, Meland origin and the locality-guide note that couples were usually married in the bride's home parish)
- **Bride's marital status (pige/enke):** Not indexed; the original may clarify whether Unna was a maiden (pige) or widow (enke) at the time of marriage. Given her birth year of 1745 and the groom's birth year of 1759, she was approximately 41 at marriage — an age that makes a prior marriage plausible, though not established.
- **Additional details (banns dates, bondsmen, farm names):** Not captured by the derivative index; available in the original Hamre kirkebøk.

The original Hamre kirkebøk 1750-1857 is the primary source underlying this derivative index. FamilySearch film 007621224 is confirmed patron-only (HTTP 403). Digitalarkivet (https://media.digitalarkivet.no) provides free browse access to the same register; a researcher-action URL has been provided (log_008) and is awaiting response. Until the researcher reports back from Digitalarkivet, the full content of the original entry — including any additional detail beyond what the derivative index captures — remains unread. The original is not permanently inaccessible; it is pending a researcher browser session.

---

### Conflicts

No conflicts are registered in the project for q_001. The 1801 census anomaly (Borni Nilsdatter as wife) is documented analytically but is a secondary question about Unna's fate, not a conflict on the core 1786 marriage facts.

---

### Tier and Limitations

This conclusion is rated **probable**. The derivative marriage index entry (src_001), a systematic compilation derived from original Lutheran parish records, records the core marriage facts (date 25 June 1786, place Hamre, Hordaland, groom Anders Monsen, bride Unna Halsteinsdatter) with no contradicting evidence and with geographic corroboration from the 1801 census. The bride's name transcription artifact is documented and does not constitute a material uncertainty. However, the original Hamre kirkebøk entry has not been read — the sole direct evidence for this marriage is a derivative source. Exhaustiveness has not been declared. The 'what does the record show' component of the question is partially answered: the indexed fields are established, but additional detail available in the original (banns, bondsmen, marital status, farm names) is pending the researcher's Digitalarkivet browse.

The tier would advance to **proved** if: (1) the researcher completes the Digitalarkivet browse and confirms (or corrects) the indexed date, place, and names from the original entry, providing a second independent attestation; and (2) exhaustiveness is declared once the original is accessed and no additional unsearched record types remain.

A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
